entries.title: Mobile Security: App Transport Security: arbitrary loads allowed
entries.description: NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true disables ATS globally; non-HTTPS connections are permitted.
entries.impact: The app may communicate with backends over plaintext HTTP; an on-path attacker can read or modify any unencrypted traffic, including authentication tokens.
entries.remediation_brief: Remove NSAllowsArbitraryLoads or scope to specific domains via NSExceptionDomains.

entries.title: Mobile Security: ATS exception allows HTTP for {dom}
entries.description: Per-domain NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads exception bypasses ATS for the listed domain.
entries.impact: Traffic to the excepted domain is plaintext and subject to interception. Acceptable only for legacy backends you control and have committed to migrating.
entries.remediation_brief: Migrate the backend to HTTPS and remove the exception.

entries.title: Mobile Security: Custom URL scheme registered: {sch}://
entries.description: Custom URL scheme allows any app on the device to invoke this app with arbitrary parameters.
entries.impact: If deep-link handlers don't validate parameters or enforce authentication, a malicious app could trigger sensitive actions (password change, in-app purchase, etc.). Verify each handler.
entries.remediation_brief: Validate every parameter; require re-authentication for sensitive actions; prefer Universal Links over custom schemes where possible.

entries.title: Mobile Security: get-task-allow enabled (debuggable binary)
entries.description: The binary's entitlements set get-task-allow=true, allowing debuggers to attach.
entries.impact: An attacker on a jailbroken device can attach lldb to the running process and read memory, dump keychain items, or modify runtime behaviour. Should never ship in App Store builds.
entries.remediation_brief: Set get-task-allow=false in the production entitlements file before signing.

entries.title: Mobile Security: Wildcard application-identifier in entitlements
entries.description: Wildcard provisioning profile (e.g. com.example.*) used in entitlements.
entries.impact: Keychain access groups and shared containers are scoped wider than intended; other apps signed with the same wildcard can read shared keychain entries.
entries.remediation_brief: Use specific bundle-identifier provisioning profiles in production.

entries.title: Information Disclosure: Potential hard-coded secret: {label}
entries.description: Pattern matching a known secret format (AWS access key, Google API key, private key, …) was found in the bundle.
entries.impact: Hard-coded secrets in client binaries are trivially recoverable by anyone with the IPA. If valid in production they grant the attacker the same privileges as the app, often including server-side actions the user is not authorised for.
entries.remediation_brief: Rotate the exposed secret; remove from the bundle; fetch via authenticated server call.
